L22: 【8†Proposition 33.45.13 (Asymptotic Riemann-Roch).】 Let $k$ be a field. Let $X$ be a proper scheme over $k$ of dimension $d$. Let $\mathcal{L}$ be an ample invertible $\mathcal{O}_ X$-module. Then
L23: 
L24: \[ \dim _ k \Gamma (X, \mathcal{L}^{\otimes n}) \sim c n^ d + l.o.t. \]
L25: 
L26: where $c = \deg _\mathcal {L}(X)/d!$ is a positive constant.
L27: 
L28: Proof. This follows from the definitions, Lemma 【14†33.45.9】, and the vanishing of higher cohomology in Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 【15†30.17.1】. $\square$

L23: 【8†Lemma 33.45.9.】 Let $k$ be a field. Let $X$ be proper over $k$. Let $Z \subset X$ be a closed subscheme of dimension $d$. If $\mathcal{L}_1, \ldots , \mathcal{L}_ d$ are ample, then $(\mathcal{L}_1 \cdots \mathcal{L}_ d \cdot Z)$ is positive.
L24: Proof. We will prove this by induction on $d$. The case $d = 0$ follows from Lemma 【15†33.33.3】. Assume $d > 0$. By Lemma 【16†33.45.6】 we may assume that $Z$ is an integral closed subscheme. In fact, we may replace $X$ by $Z$ and $\mathcal{L}_ i$ by $\mathcal{L}_ i|_ Z$ to reduce to the case $Z = X$ is a proper variety of dimension $d$. By Lemma 【17†33.45.5】 we may replace $\mathcal{L}_1$ by a positive tensor power.
L25: Thus we may assume there exists a nonzero section $s \in \Gamma (X, \mathcal{L}_1)$ such that $X_ s$ is affine (here we use the definition of ample invertible sheaf, see Properties, Definition 【18†28.27.1】). Observe that $X$ is not affine because proper and affine implies finite (Morphisms, Lemma 【19†29.45.11】) which contradicts $d > 0$. It follows that $s$ has a nonempty vanishing scheme $Z(s) \subset X$.
L26: Since $X$ is a variety, $s$ is a regular section of $\mathcal{L}_1$, so $Z(s)$ is an effective Cartier divisor, thus $Z(s)$ has codimension $1$ in $X$, and hence $Z(s)$ has dimension $d - 1$ (here we use material from Divisors, Sections 【20†31.14】, 【21†31.15】, and 【22†31.16】 and from dimension theory as in Lemma 【23†33.20.3】). By Lemma 【10†33.45.8】 we have
L27: \[ (\mathcal{L}_1 \cdots \mathcal{L}_ d \cdot X) = (\mathcal{L}_2 \cdots \mathcal{L}_ d \cdot Z(s)) \]
L28: 
L29: By induction the right hand side is positive and the proof is complete. $\square$
